arbitrated.notes:
Realised inflation is running very hot: headline CPI YoY at 5.25%, core PCE near 3.93%, 3m annualized headline at 8.17%, core at 5.70%, and YoY range position at 0.99 (near 12m high). This is a strong "hot realised inflation" signal. However, per the resolution protocol, when realised inflation is hot but expectations are more muted, I resolve toward the expectations reading rather than splitting the difference.

The expectations panel (10y breakeven) shows a much more modest picture: breakeven near 2.40%, up only 0.87pp over 252 days (a slow, grinding rise from lows), but virtually flat over the last 63 days (-0.01pp) and only modestly up over 21 days (+0.08pp). The breakeven sits near the top of its 12m range (0.86 range position) but the pace of increase has stalled — it's plateauing, not accelerating, even as realised CPI prints have kept climbing. This divergence — hot realised inflation, but expectations anchoring/plateauing — is the classic signature case per the instructions, and it should resolve toward the expectations driver (near-flat to marginally higher), not toward the hot CPI print.

Labor tightness cross-read: unemployment has fallen sharply (12m change -4.8pp, at 12m low 5.40%, Sahm gap positive), signaling a tightening labor market. This adds some support to persistent inflation dynamics (wage pressure), giving some upward lean to inflation expectations, but not enough to override the plateau evident in breakeven levels themselves.

Net: breakevens likely drift marginally higher, but the move is modest and decelerating — not a continuation of the sharp widening seen over the past year. I lean mildly positive, not strongly bullish on breakevens.

trade.rationale: Modest long breakeven: hot realised inflation partially offset by plateauing expectations and tightening labor backdrop; small net upward bias only.

arbitrated.notes:
Realised inflation is hot: headline YoY at 5.15%, core PCE YoY 3.96%, both near 12-month highs, 3m-annualized core running 4.94% — clearly elevated and near cycle peak (yoy_range_position 0.97). Labor market is tight and tightening further (unemployment at 5.10%, 12m low, sahm_gap positive but small, unrate falling 3.3pp over 12m) — this is consistent with sustained wage/demand pressure that could keep realised inflation sticky, reinforcing the hot-inflation signal via a genuine cross-read rather than a single print.

However, breakevens (the actual expectations measurement) tell a different, more contained story: 10y breakeven is 2.33%, down from a recent local high of 2.39%, with be_change_21d -0.04pp and be_change_63d -0.11pp — both negative over medium windows despite the 252d change being firmly positive (+0.56pp, reflecting the post-recovery re-rating from very low breakevens). So the recent trend in market-implied expectations is a mild rollover/consolidation, not further widening, even as realised inflation prints stay hot. This is close to the textbook divergence case: hot realised inflation, but expectations comparatively anchored/rolling over — I resolve toward the expectations reading, not a split, per instruction.

Labor tightness supports the case that inflation could stay sticky (informing persistence), which argues against believing breakevens will collapse, but does not itself argue for further widening given already-elevated core distance from target (1.96pp) that markets appear to be partially pricing already (be_distance_from_target +0.33pp, range_position 0.78 — elevated but not at highs, and now easing).

Net: mild narrowing bias in breakevens over the next month, driven by the recent-week rollover in the expectations measurement itself, tempered by tight labor keeping the downside limited.

arbitrated.notes:
Realised inflation is running hot and accelerating: headline CPI YoY at 7.17% with 3m annualized at 10.5%, core PCE YoY at 5.21% with 3m annualized 6.64%, both well above target and still rising in the trailing prints. This is the classic "hot realised, does expectations confirm?" test. Breakevens (10y) have risen from 2.38 to 2.56 over the observation window, with be_change_21d +0.12pp and be_change_63d +0.19pp — a clear, persistent uptrend, not a blip, and near the top of its 12m range (0.74 position). So unlike the anchored-expectations signature case, here expectations are actually validating and following the realised inflation surge, not staying anchored. That means I don't need to override toward anchoring — the expectations measurement itself is already moving in the same direction as realised, so the read is reinforcing rather than divergent.

Labor tightness cross-read supports this: unemployment at 3.90%, near 12m low, down 2.8pp over 12 months, sahm_gap only +0.27pp — a genuinely tight labor market consistent with persistent (not transitory/base-effect) inflation pressure, reinforcing why breakevens are climbing rather than fading. No signal here suggests base effects are about to roll off in a way that would flip the expectations trend.

Net: breakevens should continue to widen — both drivers point the same way, expectations (the higher-weighted read) confirms the realised-inflation impulse, and the labor backdrop supports persistence. Conviction is high but not maximal given breakevens are already near top of range, raising some mean-reversion risk.

Realised inflation is running very hot: headline CPI YoY at 8.57%, still accelerating (headline_3m_annualized 10.09%, core_3m_annualized 5.48%, both well above trailing YoY), and yoy_range_position at the top of its 12m range with no sign of turning yet. That is an unambiguous case for the realised-inflation driver reading higher.

But breakevens (the direct expectations measurement) are the opposite signature: 10y breakeven has actually rolled over the last three prints (2.95→2.86→2.86→2.84), be_change_21d still shows a positive slope over 21d but the most recent observations show clear deceleration/reversal from the cycle high, and be_range_position of 0.85 sits below the top of its range rather than making new highs. This is exactly the classic divergence: hot realised prints, but market-implied expectations no longer chasing the headline higher — likely already discounting base effects/Fed credibility on future disinflation.

Per the guidance, when realised inflation is hot but expectations stay/are becoming anchored (or are rolling over), we resolve toward the expectations driver rather than splitting the difference. The labour market is exceptionally tight (unemployment down to 3.70%, near 12m/multi-year lows, unrate_change_12m -2.40pp) — a tightness cross-read that would ordinarily argue for persistent wage-driven inflation and higher expectations, but it is not translating into a breakeven up-move; the breakeven series is already turning down despite tight labor and hot CPI. That reinforces the read that near-term breakeven direction is expectations-led and pointing toward flat-to-narrower, not wider.

Net: I lean modestly toward narrowing breakevens over the next month, driven by the plateauing/rolling-over expectations measurement despite hot realised CPI and tight labor, since the expectations print is the one that directly maps to the traded instrument and the mandate directs resolving toward it in this divergence case.

arbitrated.notes: Realised inflation is running hot: headline CPI y/y at 8.23%, core PCE y/y 5.59%, both near 12-month highs (range position ~0.9), 3m annualized headline still 8.8%. This is the classic hot-realised-print case. But the expectations driver — 10y breakeven — is the one that actually prices the wedge, and it is NOT confirming the realised-inflation trajectory: breakevens have been range-bound 2.85-3.02 over the last 10 observations, currently 2.88, down from a recent 2.97 peak and roughly flat over 21 days (+0.02pp) despite being up meaningfully over 63d/252d (+0.44/+0.47pp, reflecting the broad 2021-22 repricing already embedded). The recent trend (last 4 prints: 2.91, 2.85, 2.88, 2.97, 2.88) shows breakevens oscillating without a clear breakout above the 12m high of 3.02 — i.e., inflation expectations look anchored/consolidating even as realised inflation prints stay elevated. Given the expectations data explicitly shown to me is flat-to-slightly-pulled-back in the near term, and the resolution rule directs me to lean on expectations over realised persistence, I read the wedge as roughly flat with a mild upward tilt from the labor cross-read, not a strong widening call. Net: modest positive lean, low-to-moderate conviction, expectations-anchored dominates the hot realised print.

arbitrated.notes:
Realised inflation is hot and accelerating on headline (yoy at 8.98%, 3m annualized 10.5%, yoy_range_position at the top of its 12m range), though core PCE yoy has actually turned down over the last 3 months (-0.42pp) suggesting some cooling beneath the headline surge — likely energy/base-effect driven noise rather than broadening persistence. Meanwhile the market-based expectations read (10y breakeven) is unambiguously falling: down from 2.62 to 2.33 over the observed window, -0.31pp over 21 days and -0.53pp over 63 days, sitting near the bottom of its 12-month range (range_position 0.14). This is the classic divergence case — hot realised inflation against anchored-to-falling expectations — and the instruction is clear: resolve toward the expectations driver, not a split. Breakevens are a market-priced, forward-looking measure and are trending down hard and recently (not stale), so I weight this heavily.

Labor tightness offers a supportive cross-read: unemployment is at 12-month lows (3.60%), sahm_gap near zero, distance from natural negative — tight labor market. But even this tightness has not translated into rising expectations; if anything it argues wage-cost persistence, yet breakevens are falling anyway, reinforcing that the market is pricing disinflation ahead (perhaps on Fed tightening priced via curve — dgs2 up more than dgs10, curve flattening/inverting per slope readings, consistent with tightening expectations subduing future inflation).

Net: expectations driver dominates and is falling, decisively pointing to breakeven narrowing. Realised inflation stays hot but this is exactly the case where we don't chase the hot print — we follow the anchored/falling expectations signal.
arbitrated.falsifier: A rebound in breakevens back above ~2.50 alongside confirmation core inflation persistence is broadening (not just headline) would flip toward widening.

If Fed pauses tightening on growth fears, inflation expectations could re-widen despite current downtrend.
Headline CPI momentum this hot could eventually pull breakevens back up if it persists past base effects.

trade.rationale: Falling, fresh market-priced breakevens dominate over hot-but-decelerating-core realised inflation; positions for continued narrowing of the 10y inflation wedge.

why.labor_tightness: Unemployment at 12m low (3.60%), sahm_gap near zero — labor market still tightening, own measurement (unrate) falling.

Per the resolution rule, when realised inflation is (superficially) hot but expectations are visibly moving/anchoring down, we weight expectations — and here expectations aren't just anchored, they're falling outright, which is the strongest possible signal for the breakeven wedge itself (breakevens ARE expectations, nearly by definition of the instrument).

arbitrated.notes:
Realised inflation is decelerating clearly: headline CPI yoy has fallen from ~9% to 6.33%, 3m annualized headline is 3.28% (well below yoy), core PCE also drifting down (3m change -0.52pp), and both are off their 12m highs at the range floor. This is the classic disinflation-in-progress print. Labor market remains very tight (unemployment at 3.50%, near 12m low, distance from natural -0.50pp), which cross-reads as some persistence risk in services/core inflation, but tightness has been stable/plateauing (unrate_change_6m = 0.00), not accelerating — so it argues for sticky-but-not-reaccelerating inflation, not a re-widening shock.

The critical driver is expectations: 10y breakevens have been drifting down — -0.03pp over 21d, -0.21pp over 63d, -0.14pp over 252d, and sit near the low end of their 12-month range (range position 0.13). This is a fresh, non-stale reading directly measuring the wedge, and it shows compression, not anchoring at a stable level. Per the playbook, realised-inflation cooling plus expectations also cooling is not a divergence case — both signals agree on narrowing. There's no sign of hot realised inflation with anchored expectations (the classic divergence); instead we have disinflation confirmed by both actual data and market pricing.

Given the expectations measurement is the freshest and most directly on-mandate for this trade, and it corroborates the realised-inflation disinflation trend, I read this as a moderate narrowing bias for 10y breakevens. Labor tightness offers a mild upside risk to persistence but not enough to offset the clear cooling in both core drivers.

Realised inflation is decelerating clearly: headline CPI y/y has fallen from ~9% to 5.96%, core PCE y/y drifting down to 4.94%, and 3m annualized headline (3.61%) is well below the y/y print, signalling disinflation momentum via base effects and cooling sequential prints. That's the realised-inflation driver's own signature: falls, clearly.

But breakevens (the expectations driver) are not confirming that disinflation — 10y breakeven has actually crept up over 21d (+0.10pp) and 63d (+0.11pp) to 2.43%, near the top of its recent range (position 0.34, but off the 12m low), even as the 252d change is still negative (-0.10pp) reflecting the broader down-move from the 2022 peak. Near-term, expectations are stabilizing/inching higher, not falling further. This is the classic divergence: realised inflation cooling while near-term expectations stay sticky/anchored-but-not-falling. Per the resolution rule, I weight the expectations driver more heavily for the breakeven wedge itself, since breakevens ARE the expectations measurement, not a mere read on it.

Net: with realised inflation falling but expectations (breakevens) modestly firming and labor tightness intact, I lean toward a mild widening bias in breakevens over the horizon, not a narrowing — the disinflation is already priced and the marginal signal from breakevens themselves is up.

Given the panel's guidance to weight expectations most when they diverge from realised inflation: realised inflation is falling clearly, expectations are also falling on a longer window but showing tentative stabilization/small uptick recently. There's no strong divergence forcing an override — both point modestly toward continued disinflationary pressure on breakevens, with expectations dominating since they are the traded object. Net: lean toward narrower breakevens, but with softened conviction given the recent 21d/63d crosscurrents and labor tightness cross-read tempering the disinflation case somewhat.

arbitrated.notes:
Realised inflation is decelerating but still sticky at the margin: headline CPI yoy has fallen sharply from ~8-9% to ~5%, and 3m annualized headline is back to 3.27%, though core PCE yoy is still elevated (4.78%) and core 3m annualized (4.74%) shows stalled progress on the core side — a classic base-effects-down-but-core-sticky picture. That alone would be a mixed/neutral-to-slightly-positive read for realised inflation pressure on breakevens (deceleration argues for narrowing, but sticky core caps how much further it falls).

The decisive signal here is inflation expectations: 10y breakeven has fallen from 2.32 to 2.18, with consistent declines on 21d (-0.16), 63d (-0.11) and especially 252d (-0.67pp), sitting near the bottom of its 12m range (range_position 0.09). This is a clear, well-populated, non-stale series showing anchored-to-falling expectations, not anchoring at a stable level — expectations are compressing further, not diverging upward against a hot realised print. Per the resolution rule, when realised inflation is elevated/mixed but expectations are clearly falling, we resolve toward the expectations driver.

The labor market cross-read reinforces this: unemployment is at 12-month lows (3.40%), still falling (-0.30pp over 12m), signaling a tight labor market. Tight labor normally argues for persistent inflation and could support breakevens, but the breakeven series itself is already telling us the market isn't pricing that persistence — it's compressing. Given the priority the arbitration rules place on the expectations read over realised/labor cross-reads, I weight the breakeven decline heavily and expect further narrowing of the 10y inflation wedge over the horizon.
arbitrated.falsifier: A rebound in breakevens back above ~2.25-2.30 with core inflation re-accelerating and unemployment ticking up would flip this toward widening.

risks.text: Fed balance sheet swings and financial conditions easing (NFCI up 0.11 over 13w) could loosen conditions and lift inflation expectations unexpectedly.
Leveraged funds showing large negative z-scores/flow reversals could exaggerate breakeven moves on repositioning rather than fundamentals.
Sticky core PCE at 4.78% could stall further breakeven compression if realised core prints surprise hot.

trade.rationale: Breakeven series shows clear, multi-horizon decline near 12m lows; expectations dominate over mixed realised inflation and tight-labor cross-read per resolution hierarchy.

why.inflation: Headline yoy plunging, 3m annualized back to 3.3%, but core PCE and core 3m annualized still sticky ~4.7-4.8%, so mild net deceleration.
why.inflation_expectations: 10y breakeven fell from 2.32 to 2.18, clear declines across 21d/63d/252d, near 12m range bottom — clearly falling.
why.labor_tightness: Unemployment at 12m low 3.40%, falling steadily over 3/6/12m — labor market own-measurement (unrate) is falling, i.e. tightening.

arbitrated.notes:
Realised inflation is decelerating clearly: headline yoy has fallen from ~8.2% to 3.3%, 3m annualized headline is 2.35%, core 3m annualized 2.80%, and core yoy is down 0.49pp over 3m though still elevated at 4.3%. This is the disinflation base-effect story — realised inflation trending down, consistent with narrower breakevens if expectations followed. But expectations have NOT followed: 10y breakeven has risen from 2.22 to 2.37-2.39 over the period, up 0.17pp in 21d and 0.19pp in 63d, sitting near the middle of its 12m range (0.52 position) and only 0.05pp below its 12m high. This is a live, non-stale signal showing expectations drifting up even as realised inflation cools — the classic hot-realised-vs-anchored-expectations divergence, except here it's inverted: expectations are firming while realised cools. Per the resolution rule, weight the expectations driver most since the two diverge, and expectations are recent (10 obs, last obs current) not stale.

Labor tightness cross-read: unemployment rate stable at 3.5-3.6%, near 12m lows, sahm_gap trivial (+0.17), distance from natural -0.50pp — labor market still tight, which supports somewhat sticky inflation persistence and lends some credence to breakevens firming rather than collapsing, reinforcing the expectations signal rather than contradicting it.

Net read: breakevens biased to widen modestly, driven by the expectations uptrend which dominates over decelerating realised inflation. Conviction moderate — expectations move is real but not extreme (near range midpoint, only recent 21d/63d gains, 252d change slightly negative at -0.05pp suggesting the up-move is a recent reversal within a broader flat-to-down year).

arbitrated.notes:
The realised-inflation tape shows headline CPI y/y ticking up modestly over the last few prints (3.07→3.72→3.69) with a hot 3m annualized headline (4.36%) versus core cooling steadily (core PCE y/y down from 4.79 to 3.83, core 3m annualized just 2.05%). This is a classic case of headline noise (likely energy/base effects) against a decelerating core trend — the underlying persistence signal is soft, not hot. Labor tightness cross-read reinforces this: unemployment has drifted up to the top of its 12m range (3.70%, sahm_gap +0.23pp, unrate_range_position 1.00), consistent with a cooling labor market that would cap wage-driven inflation persistence rather than argue for it. So the realised-inflation picture, filtered through the labor lens, is not a genuine hot-persistence story.

The expectations panel is the key read here per the arbitration rule, and it is telling a quiet, anchored story: 10y breakeven has oscillated in a tight 2.33-2.39% band, be_change_21d/63d modestly positive (+0.09/+0.13pp) but be_change_252d is negligible (+0.02pp) and be_range_position is almost exactly mid-range (0.51). This is a stale/flat expectations signal — no directional conviction, well anchored, not chasing the headline CPI uptick.

Given the divergence rule (hot headline vs anchored expectations → resolve toward expectations, not a split), and given expectations themselves show only a marginal drift wider with weak persistence, I lean toward a small widening bias in breakevens, but with low conviction given the flat 252d change and mid-range position. This is not a strong wedge trade.
arbitrated.falsifier: A clear break of breakeven above 2.39% (12m range top) sustained over 21d, or core inflation reaccelerating alongside tightening labor data, would flip this to a stronger widening view.

arbitrated.notes:
Realised inflation is decelerating: headline CPI yoy at 3.09%, core PCE yoy at 3.16%, both down over the last 3 months (headline -0.16pp, core -0.32pp over 3m), and the 3m-annualized rates (headline 2.63%, core 3.29%) are running near or below the yoy level, signaling further disinflation ahead via base effects and soft recent prints. Labor tightness shows mild loosening (unemployment up 0.2pp over 12m, sahm_gap +0.33), a cross-read that reinforces the disinflation trend rather than an inflationary wage-price risk — this supports rather than contradicts the realised-inflation read, so no override is needed there.

The key driver here is inflation expectations, and it is unambiguous and fresh: 10y breakeven has fallen from 2.34 to 2.26 over the last ~10 observations, with 63d change -0.18pp and even the 21d change only a modest +0.10pp bounce off a lower base. Breakeven sits near the low end of its 12m range (range_position 0.38, near 12m low of 2.10) and below its longer-run distance-from-target. This is a case of realised inflation cooling AND expectations also cooling in tandem — not a divergence case requiring resolution toward one signal over the other. Both point the same direction: narrowing breakevens.

Given the panel is fresh (data extends to recent observations) and both realised and expectations readings agree directionally, I have reasonably high conviction the wedge continues to narrow modestly. The labor cross-read (softening labor market) supports continued disinflation, reinforcing the same direction, not creating tension.

why.inflation_expectations: 10y breakeven fell from 2.34 to 2.26, near 12m-low, 63d change -0.18pp; clear downward drift.
why.labor_tightness: Unemployment rising 0.2pp/12m, sahm_gap positive; loosening labor cross-read reinforces disinflation, not wage pressure.

The expectations driver — 10y breakeven — is also falling: from 2.31% down to 2.24%, with negative changes at 21d, 63d and 252d horizons, and sitting in the lower third of its 12-month range. A loosening labor market supports continued wage/inflation deceleration, reinforcing the breakeven-narrowing thesis rather than contradicting it.

All three legs — realised inflation cooling, expectations declining, labor loosening — line up in the same direction: narrowing breakevens. No divergence requiring an override; the base case is a clean, corroborated read. I'll take a confident short breakeven position.

This alignment (rather than divergence) gives more confidence than either series alone. The labor cross-read is a weak corroborating input, not a driver of reversal.

The realised-inflation panel shows a mixed but not alarming picture: headline CPI yoy ticked up to 2.68% from a 2.33% low, but the 3m annualized measures (headline and core both at 2.08%) sit well below the yoy prints, and core yoy actually fell 0.18pp over 3 months. Labor tightness is essentially flat-to-slightly-loosening: unemployment 3m avg at 4.20%, sahm_gap +0.20pp, range position only 0.33 (nearer the low end of its 12m band) — no sign of a wage-price spiral building, which supports reading the recent hot CPI prints as transitory rather than persistent.

The critical cross-read is inflation expectations, which is not stale (10 daily-ish obs, current) and shows breakevens actually declining: -0.03pp over 21d, -0.08pp over 63d, sitting at 2.29% versus a 12m range of 2.02-2.46 (61st percentile, off the highs). This is the signature divergence case: realised inflation running a bit hot/sticky at the margin while expectations stay anchored and are actually drifting down. Per the resolution rule, weight the expectations driver over the realised print when they diverge — anchored/falling expectations dominate.

Combining: soft labor market cross-read reinforces that current inflation firmness is not persistent, and directly-observed breakevens are already softening. This points to a narrowing wedge — modest, since the move is small (a few bps over weeks) and not a collapse. I lean modestly short breakevens (narrowing), not aggressively, since the data isn't extreme in either direction.

arbitrated.notes:
Realised inflation is hot: headline CPI y/y sits at 3.00% near its 12m high (range position 0.97), 3m annualized headline at 3.43%, core PCE also creeping up to 2.97% y/y with core-3m annualized 2.97%. This is a clear signature of inflation running hot on the realised side. However, the expectations driver — 10y breakeven — is not confirming this at all: breakevens are flat to slightly down, sitting at 2.24-2.25%, near the low end of their 12m range (range position 0.28), with 63d and 252d changes both -0.10pp. This is the classic divergence case: hot realised inflation but anchored/falling expectations. Per the resolution rule, weight the expectations driver over the realised one when they diverge — markets are treating the current CPI/PCE strength as transitory or base-effect driven rather than persistent, and are not repricing long-run inflation compensation.

Cross-check via labor: unemployment rate has been drifting up (4.40% latest, 3m avg 4.43%, up 0.10pp over 3m, 0.20pp over 12m, near 12m high with range position 0.80). A loosening labor market undercuts the case for sustained wage-driven inflation persistence, reinforcing the anchored-breakeven read rather than the hot-CPI read. This cross-read supports fading the realised inflation signal.

Net: breakevens are the freshest and most direct read on the actual trade instrument, and they show mild narrowing/flat-to-down trend, not widening. I lean toward modest narrowing in inflation compensation, consistent with anchored expectations and a softening labor backdrop outweighing a currently-hot but likely transient CPI print.
